text:
alice: Heads-up — noticed a 27% cost bump from GPU spend in us-west1 last week. Correlated with three spot waves + CA (cluster-autoscaler) scale-down loops. proposing a warm-pool + graceful handoff to reduce thrash.
ben: 27% yikes. Do we have a breakdown by nodegroup and preemptible vs on-demand?
priya: Quick snapshot: spot-gpu-ng-1: 60% of GPU hours; 5 preempts in 24h; autoscaler scaled down then up twice. average GPU utilization on spot nodes was 22% (lots of low-priority jobs).
carlos: TL;DR: thrash + cold model warmup time = wasted cycles. strategy idea: 1) small on-demand warm pool (5-10% of total GPU capacity) kept ready with preloaded model artifacts 2) soft-taint spot nodes so low-priority pods move when warm nodes appear 3) lifecycle hooks + termination-handler drain flow so we avoid racing with CA.
alice: Exactly. Also need to tune CA scaleDownDelay and scaleDownUnneededTime so we don't immediately drain nodes that will be reused in seconds.
priya: +1. Also set cpu/gpu utilization thresholds lower for deciding unneeded for GPU nodegroups. Right now CA looks at resource requests, not actual GPU device load, so pods with small CPU but heavy GPU may be mis-accounted.
carlos: Implementation notes: use node taint for spot: "marketplace=spot:NoSchedule" and give tolerations to batch/low-priority workloads. Warm nodes will be labeled "warmpool=true" and NOT tainted.
maria: Might be worth using a tiny warmkeeper DaemonSet on warm nodes that preloads models and keeps a small Inference container running to populate NV caches. That reduces cold-start time when we move a production pod.
infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: rollout for warmkeeper-ds started in staging at 1903456700. :white_check_mark:
ben: For AWS: we should wire EC2 lifecycle hooks -> SNS -> SQS -> node-termination-handler (or custom) to initiate cordon/drain before instance termination. That buys us ~2 minutes on spot interruption notices.
alice: + make sure we call kubelet eviction with grace longer than model checkpoint flush so jobs can checkpoint if needed. Also annotate pods with "k8s.gpu/needs-checkpoint=yes" so our drain script handles them specially.
priya: autoscaler config suggestions (snippet):

```
--scale-down-delay=15m
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--expander=least-waste
nodeGroupAutoDiscovery: true
```

This reduces flip-flopping and prefers existing capacity.
carlos: Also consider CA balancing mode: prefer to scale up on warmpool nodegroup with higher priority and only use spot as overflow. Use labels + CA node group priorities (cloud provider tags) to influence selection.
maria: Operational playbook: when interruption wave happens, prefer to move critical traffic to warmpool nodes; if warmpool exhausted, fallback to on-demand burst or postpone non-urgent jobs. Need runbooks + alerting for warmpool saturation.
ben: Cost tradeoffs: 5-10% warmpool increases reserved on-demand spend but should cut the re-provision churn and wasted GPU hours. We should model breakeven: cost_warmpool <= avoided_spinup_cost + wasted_compute. I'll run numbers.
alice: Action items:
- maria: prototype warmkeeper DaemonSet + warm nodegroup config (due end of week)
- ben: run cost breakeven model and suggested sizing (2 days)
- priya & carlos: PR for CA flags + taint/toleration policy + termination-hook wiring (this week)
- infra-bot: add alert "warmpool_capacity_low" and "spot_thrash_detected" to pager duty if >3 scale cycles in 1h
maria: ack. I'll start a staging test: create warmpool ng with 6 GPUs, deploy warmkeeper that preloads our 2 largest models and report back metrics.
ben: thanks. if anyone has objections to the soft-taint plan speak now, otherwise I'll size warmpool in the cost model with a 7% baseline.
alice: No objections from me. Let's keep node drain grace for critical pods at least 90s and PDBs enforced for stateful services. :thumbsup:
priya: one more note — for GKE preemptible we only get 30s notice sometimes; make sure our termination-handler fallback continues to work by using event-based drain and CA safeguards.
carlos: Agreed. We'll instrument with a short-lived probe that validates model warmness (latency < 50ms) before we redirect traffic.
maria: I'll post staging results in this thread when I have numbers. thanks everyone.
